title: 3.5. Sorting Algorithms & Multidimensional Lists
summary: Implement the Bubble Sort algorithm from scratch, understand list copying vs aliasing, and work with multi-dimensional matrices and list comprehensions.
learningObjectives: Implement the Bubble Sort algorithm to understand sorting mechanics and element swapping.
Recognize the critical difference between variable aliasing (a = b) and shallow copying (a = b[:]).
Process two-dimensional lists (matrices) and construct list comprehensions.

sections.heading: 3.5.1 The Bubble Sort Algorithm
sections.content:
Bubble Sort is a classic sorting algorithm that repeatedly steps through a list, compares adjacent elements, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.

In Python, swapping two elements is elegant using simultaneous assignment:
numbers[i], numbers[i + 1] = numbers[i + 1], numbers[i]

knowledgeChecks.prompt: If list_a = [1, 2, 3] and list_b = list_a, what happens when you run list_b.append(4)?

options.text: Both list_a and list_b contain [1, 2, 3, 4] because they reference the same object
Only list_b is modified; list_a remains [1, 2, 3]
A copy of list_a is automatically created

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Assignment (=) binds a new name to the existing object in memory without creating a copy.

recap: Bubble Sort demonstrates algorithmic sorting; variable assignment copies references, not list contents.
